details:
**Derek Chauvin**
The Minneapolis police officer who knelt on Floyd's neck for over nine minutes on May 25, 2020, killing him. Chauvin was convicted of murder in April 2021 and sentenced to 22.5 years in prison. Three other officers involved, Tou Thao, J. Alexander Kueng, and Thomas Lane, were also convicted of crimes.

**"I can't breathe"**
The words Floyd gasped repeatedly while Chauvin knelt on him. The phrase, also linked to the 2014 police killing of Eric Garner, became a rallying cry of the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests.

**8 minutes and 46 seconds**
The originally reported length of time Chauvin knelt on Floyd's neck. Protesters and officials, including members of Congress, observed silences or knelt for that long in his memory. Evidence at trial later showed the true length was about 9 minutes and 29 seconds.

**38th Street and Chicago Avenue (George Floyd Square)**
The Minneapolis intersection where Floyd was killed, outside the Cup Foods store. It became a community-run memorial site and was named George Floyd Square.

**Cup Foods and Mahmoud Abumayyaleh**
The corner store owned by Mahmoud Abumayyaleh where Floyd bought cigarettes just before his death. A store employee called police because he believed Floyd had paid with a counterfeit $20 bill. Security footage from the store showed the purchase.

**Statues of George Floyd**
Several statues were put up to honor Floyd after his murder. In Newark, New Jersey, a 700-pound bronze statue of him seated on a bench was placed at City Hall. In Brooklyn, artist Chris Carnabuci created a statue unveiled on Juneteenth 2021 whose inscription says that "knees should be used to pray."

**Patriot Front vandalism**
In June 2021 the white nationalist group Patriot Front vandalized two statues of Floyd in New York and New Jersey, spray-painting its name and logo on them.

**Sunflower mural**
A large mural painted at the 38th and Chicago site shortly after Floyd's death. It shows his face and name in front of a big sunflower against a blue background, and it became one of the best-known images of the memorial.

**Largest change.org petition**
The "Justice for George Floyd" petition on change.org, which demanded that the officers be arrested and charged, became the largest petition in the site's history, gathering many millions of signatures.

**#TheShowMustBePaused (Blackout Tuesday)**
A campaign started by music industry executives Jamila Thomas and Brianna Agyemang. On June 2, 2020, record labels and artists paused normal business, and millions of people posted plain black squares on social media in solidarity with Floyd and the protests.

**Juneteenth**
The June 19 holiday marking the end of slavery in the United States. The Brooklyn statue of Floyd was unveiled on Juneteenth 2021, and that same week the holiday was made a federal holiday, partly in response to the national reckoning that followed Floyd's murder.
